qs.q: Which of the following statements about GIT hormones affecting gastric function is correct?
o: A. Gastrin is the only hormone that stimulates gastric acid secretion.
C. Somatostatin acts primarily to stimulate gastrin release.
B. Secretin, CCK, and GIP all inhibit gastric acid secretion and/or motility.
D. Histamine directly inhibits parietal cell acid secretion.
qs.e: Secretin, Cholecystokinin (CCK), and Gastric Inhibitory Peptide (GIP) are all enterogastrones, hormones released from the small intestine that inhibit gastric acid secretion and/or gastric motility, to allow the small intestine time to process incoming chyme. qs.q: About the GIT hormones affecting gastric function: - (
o: Gastrin secretion is stimulated by the digestive products of fat.
GIP and VIP inhibit gastric secretion.
Gastrin inhibits gastric secretion and delays gastric emptying.
Somatostatin is a powerful stimulator to both gastric secretion and motility.
CCK and Secretin increase both gastric secretion and motility.
qs.e: GIP (Glucose-dependent Insulinotropic Peptide) and VIP both inhibit gastric secretion. CCK and secretin inhibit gastric function, while gastrin stimulates it.

qs.q: Regarding the GIT hormones affecting gastric function, which statement is TRUE?
o: GIP is primarily involved in protein digestion.
Gastrin is inhibited by high gastric pH.
qs.e: Secretin is released in response to acid and inhibits gastric acid secretion. Gastrin is stimulated by increased gastric pH. CCK slows gastric emptying. GIP (Gastric Inhibitory Peptide) is involved in regulating gastric secretion and motility, not primarily protein digestion.
qs.s: Weekly Year 2: GIT Physiology Exam - May 29, 2026 (Section A: MCQs)

qs.q: Regarding GIT hormones affecting gastric function, which statement is correct?
qs.e: Gastrin is a potent stimulator of gastric acid secretion from parietal cells. CCK and secretin generally inhibit gastric emptying and acid secretion, while GIP also inhibits gastric emptying.
qs.s: Weekly Year 2: GIT Physiology Exam - May 15, 2026 (Section A: MCQs)

qs.q: About the GIT hormones affecting gastric function, which is correct?
o: GIP (Gastric Inhibitory Peptide) stimulates insulin release
qs.e: GIP, also known as Glucose-dependent Insulinotropic Peptide, stimulates insulin release from the pancreas in response to glucose.

qs.q: Regarding GIT hormones affecting gastric function, which statement is true?
qs.e: CCK inhibits gastric emptying to ensure adequate time for fat digestion in the duodenum.
qs.s: Weekly Year 2: GIT Physiology Exam - April 3, 2026 (Section A: MCQs)

qs.q: Which of the following gastrointestinal hormones primarily affects gastric function by inhibiting it?
qs.e: Both CCK and Secretin are released from the duodenum in response to chyme, and both inhibit gastric emptying and acid secretion, providing negative feedback to the stomach (part of the intestinal phase of gastric regulation). Gastrin stimulates gastric function. Motilin stimulates motility during fasting.
